ROLL CALL: At 6:40 p.m., on Monday, February 12, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, MAZA
PRESENT via videoconference:  ANDRADE-STADLER
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Police Chief Kennedy, Fire Chief
Ragusa

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

PUBLIC HEARING

2.  ORDINANCE AMENDING THE ZONING CODE TO ALLOW MEDICINAL CANNABIS
  DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS IN THE INDUSTRIAL ZONE WITH A CONDITIONAL USE
  PERMIT AND REGULATORY BUSINESS PERMIT TO IMPLEMENT THE REQUIREMENTS
  OF SB 1186 – F2M23-78, N2M24-7, O2M24-4826

  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M24-7 for the City Council to hold a public
  hearing to consider adoption of an ordinance amending the City’s Zoning Code to allow
  medicinal cannabis delivery-only retailers in the Industrial Zone with a conditional use permit
  and a regulatory business permit to implement the requirements of SB 1186. City Attorney
  MONTES delivered a staff report. The California Legislature adopted Senate Bill 1886 (“SB
  1186”) in 2022, entitled the Medicinal Cannabis Patients’ Right of Access Act, which precluded
  cities and counties from adopting or enforcing regulations that prohibit or have the effect of
  prohibiting the retail sale of medicinal cannabis by delivery. SB 1186 took effect on January 1,
  2024. SB 1186 allowed cities and counties to adopt and enforce reasonable regulations on
  the retail sale by delivery of medicinal cannabis, including zoning requirements. The City
  Council adopted an interim urgency ordinance on December 11, 2023, that was consistent
  with the proposed ordinance. The interim urgency ordinance was adopted to get regulations
  in place by the January 1, 2024 deadline while the City finished the process of adopting the
  comprehensive Zoning Code update. On January 22, 2024 the City Council extended the
  urgency ordinance for ten months and fifteen days. Now that the new Zoning Code was
  adopted, the City Council could move forward with the proposed amendment. The proposed
  ordinance would allow a delivery-only retailer of medicinal cannabis to be a conditionally
  permitted use in the Industrial zone. The retailer must only sell medicinal cannabis; the retail
  sale of adult-use (e.g., recreational) cannabis would remain prohibited. As a delivery-only
  business, there would be no storefront operations (no walk-in customers). The proposed
  ordinance also included separation requirements for such businesses. The ordinance also
  proposed that an annual business regulatory permit be required for such businesses. The
  proposed ordinance included operational standards for these businesses. These included
  security requirements, odor control measures, and a requirement that product not be visible
  from the exterior of the property. Failure to comply with the operational requirements could
  result in the regulatory permit being suspended, revoked or not renewed.

  Open & Close Public Hearing:  Mayor Maza opened the public hearing, and as there
  was no one who wished to speak, closed the same.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. MONTES clarified that these
  businesses would be located in the industrial zone, that the public would not be able to walk
  in, that purchases would be online only, that the businesses would have to verify the age of
  the purchaser, and that the businesses would still have to meet zoning distance requirements
  of being near schools. Vice Mayor PÉREZ and Mr. MONTES clarified that that there would not
  be any growers under this ordinance.

  Action Taken:  City Council conducted a public hearing and, after receiving public
  testimony, the Mayor closed the public hearing and the City Council declared introduced for
  its first reading the following ordinance entitled:

  2
2-12-24
   Ordinance No. O2M24-4826: An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of
  Alhambra adopted pursuant to the City’s Police powers and Business
  Professions Code §26320 to amend Alhambra Municipal Code Section
  23.05.020 (Land Use Regulations – Commercial Zoning Districts), Section
  23.06.020 (Land Use Regulations – Employment Zoning Districts), and
  Section 23.22.080 (Cannabis Facilities, Cultivation, and Deliveries), to
  implement California law governing Medicinal Cannabis Delivery-Only
  retailers within the City

  which ordinance would return for a second reading and adoption at the next regular City
  Council meeting.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATION

3.  ADOPTION OF THE BICYCLE AND PEDESTRIAN IMPROVEMENT PLAN;
  AUTHORIZATION TO REALLOCATE MEASURE R FUNDS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION
  OF BICYCLE AND PEDESTRIAN PLAN PROJECTS; AND ACCEPTANCE OF
  ENVIRONMENTAL EXEMPTION DETERMINATION – F2M22-33, M2M24-27

  On January 8, 2024, staff presented the Bike and Pedestrian Improvement Plan for the
  Council’s consideration, pursuant to data collection, a needs assessment, and public
  engagement conducted throughout the Plan process. This Plan is a directive under the City’s
  Strategic Plan under the goals of Enhancing Public Safety, Improving Infrastructure and
  Mobility, and Promoting Sustainability. The Plan presented on January 8, 2024 was not
  adopted by the Council; rather, based on public comment for additional time to review the
  document, consideration to adopt the Plan was tabled to the February 12th meeting. Staff and
  the City’s consultant conducted a virtual workshop on January 23, 2024; a Special Meeting
  with the Transportation Commission on January 24, 2024; and an in-person workshop at the
  Library on February 1, 2024. On January 24, 2024, the Transportation Commission submitted
  a recommendation to adopt the Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvement Plan, contingent on also
  aligning the Plan with Metro’s recent update to their Active Transportation Plan (for regional
  connectivity benefits) and removing the McLean Bridge from the City’s pedestrian or bicycle
  network.

  Councilmember MALONEY and Vice Mayor PÉREZ, as members of the City Council
  Subcommittee, delivered a report regarding the recent meetings, requests received by the
  public for additional time to receive feedback from groups partnered with the City as they
  continue to gather information. Mr. MALONEY requested that Council continue the item to a
  future meeting. Ms. PÉREZ stated that groups such as API Forward were conducting their
  own public input sessions and that they needed more flexibility to complete their process. She
  requested that the item be continued to March 11, 2024. She provided information as to how
  the public could interact with API Forward and provide further feedback. Mr. MALONEY
  requested that Council allow public to make comment at this meeting.

  Public Comment:

  The following people made suggestions regarding traffic and pedestrian safety:

  1) Jennifer Ng, S. Cordova St., also made additional suggestions regarding traffic safety
  specifically at the intersection of Cordova and Main Streets.
  3
2-12-24
   2) Xana Hermosillo, 225 Palmetto Dr. also made additional suggestions regarding traffic and
  pedestrian safety and for funding sources
  3) Efrain Mejia, 304 N. 4th St., also expressed concerns regarding the plan’s ability to address
  the danger to pedestrians.
  4) Esther Tam also spoke regarding the public outreach conducted by API Forward.
  5) Lewis McCammon, 105 N. Cordova St., distributed handouts to Council, a copies of which
  are on file in the City Clerk’s Office, and also made additional suggestions regarding traffic
  safety and the pedestrian priority zone at the intersection of Cordova and Main Streets.

  The following people spoke in favor of the Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvement Plan:

  1) Steve Placido, 1708 Edgewood Dr., representing the Transportation Commission, also
  supported further traffic studies and revisiting the Plan after adoption to evaluate its
  efficacy.
  2) Victor Dorado, 901 Novelda Rd.
  3) Thanos Trezos, 412 Story Pl., also expressed concern with the Council’s delay for
  approval.
  4) Mike Lawrence also made suggestions for additional funding for a more robust plan and
  emphasized the need for quick approval.
  5) Melissa Michelson, via Zoom, specifically supported the full Bicycle Plan.
  6) Je-Show Yang, also made additional suggestions regarding traffic safety
  7) Veronica Alvarez, via Zoom, also made additional suggestions regarding traffic safety.
  8) Jean Park, via Zoom
  9) Cliff Bender, via Zoom, also made additional suggestions regarding funding.

  Additional Comment:

  1) Scott Mason, via Zoom, made racist and antisemitic comments unrelated to Item 3.
  2) Mr. Shaner, via Zoom, made racist and antisemitic comments unrelated to Item 3.

  Discussion:  Vice Mayor PÉREZ apologized to the public for having to hear the racist
  comments.

  Ms. PÉREZ went on to address comments regarding quick approval and conducting more
  public outreach and alternative funding sources which may not be readily available or have
  already been reallocated. She emphasized Council’s effort to take this to action as soon as
  possible. Ms. PÉREZ and City Manager BINNQUIST further discussed Measure R funds and
  the process of utilizing them for this project and collaboration with METRO. She urged the
  public to continue to provide input.

  Councilmember MALONEY reiterated Ms. Pérez’s comments and stated that continuing the
  item was not a delay tactic, but that they wanted to ensure that the public had the ability to
  provide input. Mr. MALONEY motioned to continue the item.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER also acknowledged the racist comments and called for
  an end to hate speech. She went on to support the Plan and supported further engagement
  with the community. She referred to the beginning of the 2024 Strategic Planning session and
  assured the public that Council would continue to address issues within the City. She
  acknowledged the loss of funding for projects on Fremont Ave, but reiterated the City’s
  commitment to the adoption of the Plan.

  Councilmember LEE supported continuing the discussion after receiving additional public
  input, and specifically receiving input from residents for whom English was not a primary
  language. She acknowledged the necessity of the Plan but added that she had concerns
  regarding some of the streets identified for bike lanes. She agreed with Mr. Placido’s
  suggestion for more traffic studies and expressed concerns over the removal of parking spaces
  4
2-12-24
   and additional traffic lanes. She stressed that the Plan should not have a negative impact on
  residents, homeowners or business owners. She reiterated the need for a traffic study and
  parking impact study. She continued to discuss her concerns with high comfort level biking
  lanes and class 4 bike lanes.

  Ms. PÉREZ and Ms. BINNQUIST clarified the process of adopting the Plan, the process of
  executing the various projects under other contracts, and the process of including traffic
  studies under each individual project. Ms. LEE and City Attorney MONTES discussed the
  exemption from CEQA for some of the improvements proposed, environmental impacts – such
  as parking, and the ability to request such studies during the Notice Inviting Bids process. Mr.
  MONTES further clarified the process to adopt the Plan.

  Ms. LEE and Ryan JOHNSON, Project Manager from consultant Alta Planning + Design,
  further discussed the Class 4 Separated Bike Lanes, Class 2B Buffer Bike Lanes, and Class
  3 Bike Lanes. Ms. LEE reiterated that there was more work to be done in studying the impact
  of the Plan on specific areas of business or residential areas.

  Ms. LEE and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the process for the public to request traffic studies
  for specific areas in the City. Ms. LEE and Ms. PÉREZ continued to discuss traffic studies and
  the scope of the Plan. Ms. LEE and Ms. PÉREZ went on to discuss the removal of the McLean
  Bridge recommendation and other revisions made to the Plan based on public comment as
  well as the continued public input process. Ms. LEE requested that before the item returns,
  that the Subcommittee consider the bike lanes in relation to street parking and their safe
  placement.

  Mayor MAZA addressed the racist comments and apologized to the public for having to hear
  them.

  Action Taken:  City Council accept the Council Subcommittee’s request to continue
  the item for further discussion at the regular City Council meeting on March 11, 2024 at 6:00
  p.m.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 4 – 23)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda were considered by the City Council to be routine were
enacted by one motion.

4.  AUTHORIZE RFP: WATER QUALITY TESTING LABORATORY SERVICES – F2M21-29,
  RFP2M24-2

  The City of Alhambra, as the operator of a community water system, was required by the State
  Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) to conduct a variety of sampling and analytical
  analyses for drinking water. The City was also required to perform analyses for various
  constituents in accordance with several permits issued by the Los Angeles County Sanitation
  District and Regional Water Quality Control Board. All tests must be performed in a certified
  laboratory which meets State standards. City staff elected not to approve the final one-year
  contract extension of the existing contract due to unsatisfactory service. The Request for
  Proposals (RFP) would provide a one-year contract for Fiscal Year 2024-2025 with the option
  to renew for three one-year terms, if services were satisfactory.
  5
2-12-24
   Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  (RFP) to qualified firms for Water Quality Testing Laboratory Services, with proposals due no
  later than 4:00 p.m. on March 14, 2024.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE
  SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON ALMANSOR STREET – F2M23-74,
  RPF2M23-29, C2M24-9, M2M24-17

  On November 13, 2023, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  RFP2M23-29 for professional engineering design services for the Sewer Main Replacement
  Project on Almansor Street. Staff reviewed a total of four proposals. West and Associates
  Engineering, Inc. was selected based on their distinguished qualifications, experience,
  reputation, responsiveness, availability, and cost.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and West and
  Associates Engineering, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $43,500 for engineering design
  services for the Sewer Main Replacement Project on Almansor Street; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-17)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING AN APPLICATION FOR THE
  WATERSMART WATER AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY GRANT PROGRAM – F2M24-18,
  R2M24-2

  The WaterSMART Water and Energy Efficiency Grants for fiscal year 2024-2025 was
  accepting application for projects that would result in quantifiable water savings, implement
  renewable energy components, and support broader sustainability benefits. Staff planned to
  apply for a grant of up to $500,000 to replace water meters at various locations in the City to
  AMI meters. As required by the grant guidelines, the City would contribute an additional match
  of at least $500,000. The match would be covered by the Water Fund (Fund 401), if awarded.
  The grant guidelines required an official resolution by the City Council which provided authority
  to proceed with the application of projects and receipt of grant funds pursuant to the Bureau
  of Reclamation’s policies and procedures. If the project was selected for funding, staff would
  return to the City Council for approval to solicit bids or proposals, appropriate grant funds for
  the proposed projects, and issue notices of completion.

  Discussion:  None.

  6
2-12-24
   Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution R2M24-2 entitled: A Resolution of
  the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California approving the authority to file an application
  with the United States Bureau of Reclamation for the WaterSMART Water and Energy
  Efficiency Grant Program; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the
  Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  ACCEPTANCE OF ADDITIONAL GRANT FUNDS FROM THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  REGIONAL PARK AND OPEN SPACE DISTRICT (RPOSD) UNDER MEASURE A ANNUAL
  ALLOCATION GRANT PROGRAM FOR PLAYGROUND REPLACEMENT PROJECTS AT
  GRANADA PARK AND ALHAMBRA PARK – F2M21-18, M2M24-18

  On November 8, 2021, the City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M21-46 that enabled staff
  to apply for annual allocation grant funding under Measure A. On March 1, 2022, staff
  submitted an application for $687,000 to replace aging play equipment and surfacing at
  Alhambra Park and Granada Park. The application was approved for funding. Since then, the
  project costs have greatly increased, due to nationwide inflation and a shortage of construction
  materials caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Updated project costs, based on quotes
  received from a qualified vendor, nearly double the original budget. Staff requested, and was
  later approved for, additional funds in the amount of $513,000 under RPOSD’s Measure A
  Annual Allocation in order to cover the increased project costs. With the additional funding,
  staff would be able to deliver on all project components for a total grant amount of $1,200,000.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted additional grant funds in the amount of $513,000
  from the Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District (RPOSD) under the
  Measure A Annual Allocation Grant Program for the Playground Replacement Projects at
  Granada Park and Alhambra Park; appropriated revenue and expenditure funds; authorized
  the City Manager, or designee, to execute all documents related to grant implementation; and
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-18)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  ACCEPTANCE OF A GRANT AND AUTHORIZATION TO CIRCULATE A NOTICE INVITING
  BIDS FOR THE ALHAMBRA PARK BANDSHELL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT – F2M24-18,
  F2M24-22, N2M24-18, M2M24-19

  On November 8, 2021, the City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M21-46 which enabled
  staff to apply for grants funded under Measure A annual allocation. Subsequently, on
  December 11, 2023, staff submitted an application for $110,200 in grant funding for the
  Alhambra Park Bandshell Improvement Project. On January 16, 2024, the application was
  approved, and the fully executed grant agreement was issued on January 22, 2024.
  Specifications and bid documentation were prepared for the Alhambra Park Bandshell
  Improvement Project. The project included the repainting of the bandshell and stage areas

  7
2-12-24
   and installation of new fencing around the stage. Staff sought to solicit bids from prospective
  contractors for the project.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted a grant in the amount of $110,200 from the Los
  Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District (RPOSD) under the Measure A
  Annual Allocation Grant Program; appropriated revenue and expenditure funds; authorized
  the City Manager, or designee, to execute all documents related to grant implementation;
  authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to prospective contractors for the Alhambra
  Park Bandshell Improvement Project; and directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-19)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: ALMANSOR COURT EXTERIOR IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
  – F2M23-41, C2M23-46, M2M24-20

  On June 26, 2023, the City Council awarded a contract to Tom’s Construction in the amount
  $299,215 for the Almansor Court Exterior Improvement Project. There was one change order
  to the project. The change order included: painting of the banquet hall's metal/plastic rear glass
  section, repairing rusted metal gates, replacing broken roof tile, painting metal bollards; and,
  removing and repouring concrete in the path of travel areas. The change order totaled
  $47,500, which brought the contract to $346,715. Staff inspected this project, and all work
  was completed in accordance with the City’s requirements and specifications. As such, it would
  be appropriate for the City Council to accept this project as complete.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of Tom’s Construction for the Almansor
  Court Exterior Improvements Project as complete in the amount of $346,715; directed the City
  Clerk to file a Notice of Completion with the County of Los Angeles for recordation; instructed
  the Finance Director to release the 5 percent retention 35 days from the date of recordation if
  no liens are filed; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s
  action. (M2M24-20)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE, DELIVERY AND INSTALLATION OF FURNITURE,
  FIXTURES AND EQUIPMENT AT THE POLICE DEPARTMENT – F2M23-64, RFP2M23-28,
  C2M24-10, M2M24-21

  On November 13, 2023, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  (RFP) for the purchase, delivery and installation of furniture, fixtures, and equipment for the
  Police Department facility. On December 27, 2023, the City received two proposals. Four
  Police Department employees evaluated and ranked the responding proposals in accordance
  with the criteria stated in the RFP. One proposal did not include the required payment of
  8
2-12-24
   prevailing wages. The proposal received from Bask met all requirements of the evaluation
  criteria stated in the RFP including quality and completeness of submitted proposal, project
  timeline and implementation plan, fee proposal, qualifications, and experience with similar
  types of efforts.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Bask in an amount up to $133,554.35 for professional
  services to furnish sections of the Police Department; authorized the Chief of Police to execute
  said agreement; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize City Council’s
  action. (M2M24-21)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

11.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: MEN'S RESTROOM REMODEL AT THE ALHAMBRA CITY YARD
  PUBLIC WORKS BUILDING – F2M20-66, N2M24-19

  The Alhambra City Yard is a multi-functional facility located at 900 S. New Avenue. The
  restrooms in the Public Works building were in need of renovation and repairs. In addition to
  retrofitting for ADA compliance, the City planned to install water efficient fixtures, energy
  efficient lighting, a janitorial closet, and needed repairs to the facilities.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to
  prospective contractors for the Men’s Restroom Remodel Project at the Alhambra City Yard
  Public Works building; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the
  Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

12.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: ASBESTOS ABATEMENT AT THE FORMER LIBRARY
  SATELLITE BUILDING – 2025 SOUTH FREMONT AVENUE – F2M24-23, N2M24-20

  Staff applied for, and was awarded funding with assistance from Assemblymember Mike Fong
  to expand green space, in accordance with the City Council’s Strategic Plan objectives, by
  constructing a pocket park at the former library satellite building. The grant agreement with
  the State was fully executed, and all funds for the project would be disbursed by June 30,
  2026. LEAD TECH Environmental conducted professional asbestos and lead paint
  assessment services for the site and identified asbestos-containing materials. The planned
  scope of work included: removal of Roof Penetration Mastic; removal of Duct Mastic; and,
  removal of 12” X 12” Vinyl Floor Tiles and Mastic throughout the building. Project bids were
  due no later than 10:30 a.m. on March 14, 2024, in the office of the City Clerk and will be
  opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Discussion:  None.
  9
2-12-24
   Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to
  prospective contractors to abate asbestos from the former Library Satellite building located at
  2025 South Fremont Avenue; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  the Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

13.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: INSTALLATION OF LED LIGHTING AND CONTROL LINK AT
  THE ALHAMBRA DRIVING RANGE – F2M23-63, C2M23-70, M2M24-22

  On August 28, 2023, the City Council awarded a contract to Musco Lighting LLC to install LED
  Lighting and a Control-Link at the Alhambra Driving Range in the amount of $142,668.25.
  There were no change orders to the project. Staff inspected this project, and all work was
  completed in accordance with the City’s requirements and specifications. As such, it would be
  appropriate for the City Council to accept this project as complete.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of Musco Lighting LLC for the
  installation of LED Lighting and Control-Link at the Alhambra Driving Range as complete in

  On April 25, 2022, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. O2M22-4803 approving a Military
  Equipment Use Policy (“Policy”) pursuant to assembly Bill 481 (“AB 481”). In accordance with
  the legislation and the Policy, a military equipment report must be submitted to the City Council
  annually for each type of military equipment approved within one year of approval, and
  annually thereafter for as long as the military equipment is available for use. Alhambra’s 2023
  Annual Military Equipment Report, proposed 2024 military equipment purchases, and the
  Police Department’s updated policy were outlined in the Chief of Police’s staff report dated
  February 12, 2024. AB 481 requires that the Council determine, based on the annual military
  equipment report submitted pursuant to Section 7072, whether each type of military equipment
  identified in that report has complied with the standards for approval set forth in Government
  Code section 7071(d). Staff reviewed Department records and determined there were no
  complaints or concerns reported on the use of the equipment in 2023. Additionally, the
  Department conducted an internal audit and determined that there were no violations of the
  Military Equipment Use Policy.

  R2M24-3, M2M24-24

  An assessment of current personnel staffing levels in the Parks and Recreation Department
  demonstrated a need for additional positions to be filled, created, altered or moved. The Parks
  and Recreation Department had two budgeted vacant full-time positions - Clerical Assistant III
  and Park Worker I. By using the combined fully burdened funding of both positions, the Parks
  and Recreation Department could add a full-time Parks Supervisor and a Clerical Assistant II.

  provide enhanced quality programming and maintenance of the City’s parks and facilities at

  reorganization. The cost savings of the vacant positions would offset the salary of a Parks
  Supervisor and Clerical Assistant II.

  The Alhambra Municipal Code (“AMC”) is a comprehensive gathering of ordinances adopted
  by the City Council covering a wide range of topics, such as City organization, parking, land
  use, licensing, purchasing, and contracting. From time-to-time updates are made to the AMC
  to address new state legislation, clarify ambiguous provisions, or delete outdated language.
  While some of these changes require immediate consideration by the Council, most can be
  addressed periodically. Accordingly, staff intended to annually bring a code clean up
  ordinance to the Council in the first quarter of each year that would address modifications
  needed due to new legislation, as well as other suggested clarifying changes. For this first
  such annual review, City staff suggested minor changes to the AMC to reflect current practices,
  clarify confusing parts of the AMC, and bring outdated sections into compliance with State
  law. The City reviewed the environmental impacts of this Ordinance under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq. “CEQA”) and the
  regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA
  14
2-12-24
   Guidelines”). This Ordinance was not subject to further review environmental review because:
  (1) it would not result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the
  environment (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15060(c)(2); (2) there was no possibility that this
  Ordinance would have a significant effect on the environment (14 Cal. Code Regs. §
  15061(b)(3)); and (3) the Ordinance, by itself, did not constitute a “project” as defined in section
  21065 of the Public Resources Code and the CEQA Guidelines (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15378).
